instruction: Turn the image at /home/user/OIP.jpg 90 degrees clockwise and save it as 'receipt_rotated.jpg' on your Desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires rotating the receipt image 90 degrees clockwise and saving to Desktop. Evaluator verifies: (1) output file exists, (2) dimensions are swapped from original (width/height become height/width), and (3) pixel-level comparison confirms 90-degree clockwise rotation by checking that sample points from the original image match their expected positions in the rotated image according to the clockwise rotation formula: original[y,x] -> rotated[x, original_width-1-y].

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: file existence, 90-degree rotation, and clockwise direction
Getter uses correct clockwise rotation formula: original[y,x] -> rotated[x, original_width-1-y] (image.py:108-110)
Dimension swap verification ensures rotation occurred (image.py:84-87)
Pixel-level comparison with 5 sample points (corners + center) and 80% threshold distinguishes clockwise from counter-clockwise rotation (image.py:95-127)
Metric correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule' by directly accessing 'is_rotated_90' key without intermediate 'rules' access (image.py:22)
Edge cases handled: missing original file fallback (image.py:42-59), JPEG compression tolerance (image.py:116-118)
Complete semantic coverage: verifies both that rotation happened AND that it's specifically clockwise, not just any 90-degree rotation
